notes: T908 (why does a lane with 169,307 readable output tokens render UNKNOWN?) — answered: the dashboard had two sources of truth for one table. The PROGRESS row list came from live processes (pgrep); the token-reading set came from the store's in_progress rows. A lane whose store status was `done` while its worker was still alive (the T786 incident — the worker closed its own row and kept working) was LISTED by the process scan but NEVER READ, so the rate column said UNKNOWN about the lane with the most readable data in the fleet. That is the S11 defect class exactly: a surface reporting 'I cannot determine' when what it means is 'I was not asked'. The seat's first three hypotheses (provider difference, event shape, process staleness) were falsified by measurement before the verified root cause held — correction 2 in the bundle. FIX (untracked/watch-fleet.sh): the reading set is now store-in_progress UNION the live process set, so every PROGRESS row has its transcript read (the row list and the reading set share one source). A live process whose store row is NOT in_progress — the closed-but-alive state — renders the stated reason `closed` in the rate slot (not a number: the store says this run is over, and quoting its tokens/s as live progress would be the fabricated figure the S11 contract forbids) and STILL renders the transcript freshness (the worker IS still writing — the incident signal). rate_of's 'never 0' rule is unchanged for in_progress rows. The over-count control (arm C) confirms the real provider fixtures (deepseek-real from T786's session id 01a03583-..., ollama-real from T764's session id 01a03592-...) are per-turn (non-monotonic output sequence), so the sum IS the correct arithmetic and no over-count arises on real data; the cumulative-synthetic fixture (true total 1300, naive sum 3000) documents the over-count boundary no real provider reaches (correction 2 verified all four live lanes are per-turn; no cumulative-detection heuristic is added — it would risk under-counting a coincidentally-non-decreasing per-turn stream, 'confidently incorrect', the worse failure mode). RED-first evidence: tools/regression-live-rate.sh arm D fails UNKNOWN on the pre-fix watch-fleet.sh (rate='UNKNOWN', freshness='-') and passes `closed` + a fresh transcript age on the fix; arms A/B/C/E pass on both (the bug was isolated to the closed-but-alive state). The regression is wired into build.zig and passes in the build context (active fleet workers on the host do not interfere — the per-row lsof cwd check isolates scratch lanes, and wait_prog_row polls past the lsof race). Did NOT touch the underlying fleet-discipline defect (a worker that closes its own row and keeps working past its close) — that has its own row; T908 reports only what the dashboard should do when it encounters the state. Did NOT add a third real provider fixture: only two provider shapes exist in the live session corpus (both pi-jsonl, deepseek and ollama); correction 2 found no openrouter/claude lane with a live session to capture (WEIZIGO_CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_DIR unset on this host), and none was synthesised (the brief forbids synthesising the shape). The sibling regression-watch-fleet.sh arms F and G (the T493 process-filter collision arms) fail on BOTH the pre-fix and post-fix watch-fleet.sh — they are pre-existing flaky races in a script the sweep contract already excludes (it times out at the 300s watchdog), not caused by this change; arms A-E and H-T pass with the fix. Identifier: glm-5.2/T908.2. Directives read: D091 (correction 2, the verified root cause) and D094 (amend, 2026-08-25T01:49:53Z) — both acted on. D094: the operator reported the claude lane (T912/opus) still shows UNKNOWN; per T891 amendment 3 the claude lane has no --session but the Claude Code harness writes a complete growing JSONL transcript at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl, session_id from the run record (T552). Extended the meter-join (untracked/watch-fleet.sh) to read that transcript: for a task in the reading set with no pi/ollama transcript, it reads the run record's session_id, opens ONLY <claude_dir>/<session_id>.jsonl (never scans — the dir holds every claude session on the machine, D094 CAUTION), and sums message.usage.output_tokens deduped by message.id (claude session lines repeat per content block — verified: T912's session dedup sum 102681 == its envelope tokens_out 102681; naive sum 211787 over-counts 2x). arm F of tools/regression-live-rate.sh pins this with a captured real claude fixture (claude-real.jsonl, 6 lines / 2 distinct ids, dedup true total 457 vs naive sum 1371, a 3x over-count the dedup prevents). GAP — the running-claude-lane rate is structurally unavailable: the runner writes session_id to the run record only at FINALIZE (tools/runner line 804, in _finalize_run_record), so a lane whose worker is still alive (the closed-but-alive state T912 hit, or any in-flight lane) has session_id=null in its launch run record and the dashboard cannot resolve the transcript path — it renders UNKNOWN, the honest answer (never a fabricated scan). Closing that gap needs a runner-side live session_id write (a tools/runner change, which T908 does not hold — T908 holds untracked/watch-fleet.sh and tools/regression-live-rate.sh); the dashboard side is in place and will render the rate once a session_id is present. Recommended follow-up: a task holding tools/runner to write session_id to the run record during the run (or to a side-channel the dashboard reads). T912 itself is now `done` in the store (closed 2026-08-25T02:09:48Z, verdict pass) — its run record finalized with session_id 912adb11-..., but its worker had already exited, so it is no longer the live UNKNOWN case; the regression's arm F covers the mechanism deterministically.
